beliefs.practice: Use a single shared MongoClient instance per process (singleton) and reuse it across FastAPI lifetimes instead of creating a new client per request; configure sensible connection pool parameters (maxPoolSize) via the driver.
Read the DocumentDB/Mongo connection string from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) and never hard-code it or write it to logs; keep only a .env.example with a placeholder in repo.

Store/rotate the connection string and any credentials in a secret store (Azure Key Vault) and grant the app minimal access to retrieve them at runtime rather than embedding credentials in configuration files.
Ensure TLS is enforced for all client connections (use tls=true / ssl=true and require TLS 1.2+) to protect credentials and data in transit.
Use retryable writes and implement client-side retry logic with exponential backoff for transient network or throttling (429/RequestRateTooLarge) errors when running aggregations or snapshot writes.

Provision throughput appropriate for heavy aggregations: use autoscale or dedicated throughput for the database/collections used by snapshot generation (or run snapshots during low-traffic windows) to avoid RU throttling.

Choose a partition/shard key with high cardinality and even distribution (e.g., customer_id) for collections containing events; avoid using acquisition month as the primary partition key because it causes hot/large partitions.

Create appropriate indexes used by the cohort aggregation: at minimum a time-series-friendly index on event timestamp (e.g., {customer_id: 1, event_time: 1}) and index on acquisition_date/acquisition_month to speed $bucket and range filters.

When using vector search, create a vector index using the provided index type (HNSW/DiskANN/IVF) with tuned parameters (e.g., HNSW: m and efConstruction, and efSearch at query time) and store vector dimensionality and similarity metric consistently.

Use aggregation pipeline stages rather than mapReduce or server-side JavaScript for cohort computations; verify pipeline performance with explain() and ensure index usage for stages that can benefit from them.

Materialize heavy cohort snapshots as compact summary documents (one document per cohort snapshot) and refresh them on a schedule; perform snapshot writes with bulk operations to reduce RU and client-server roundtrips.

Use a lightweight distributed lock or lease based on the DB (findOneAndUpdate with a timestamp and owner id) to ensure only one snapshot job runs at a time and to avoid overlapping scheduled snapshot runs.
Limit fields returned by queries and aggregation ($project early) to only those required by the API to reduce network bandwidth and RU consumption (project before expensive stages when possible).

Design the events schema to embed frequently-accessed attributes (channel, product) inside event documents to avoid $lookup joins; if joins are required, ensure joined fields are indexed and pipeline uses $lookup efficiently or precompute denormalized snapshots.
Add TTL indexes for ephemeral event data that can be expired (e.g., raw telemetry older than X days) to control storage growth and reduce long-term RU costs.
Use explain() and the provider's profiling/monitoring (queryStats, indexUsage, RU metrics) to validate that aggregation stages hit indexes and to identify high-RU pipeline stages for optimization.

Avoid large in-memory accumulations in the aggregation pipeline (unbounded $group outputs) — use $bucket/$bucketAuto to bound group cardinality and consider incremental snapshotting for extremely large datasets.

Use bulkWrite with ordered=False for inserting/updating many documents (snapshot materialisation) to maximize throughput and reduce RU costs; handle duplicate-key errors or transient failures explicitly.
Restrict network access to the DocumentDB cluster using firewall rules, VNet integration or private endpoints; do not expose the cluster to the public internet without access controls.

Instrument the service to collect application-level metrics (snapshot duration, RU consumed per snapshot, aggregation latencies) and alert on RU throttling, high latency, or repeated failures so snapshots and API reliability can be monitored and tuned.

Set a safe write concern and reasonable wtimeout for critical writes (snapshot writes) and handle write concern errors; do not assume default fire-and-forget semantics for important materialized snapshot persistence.
When designing indexes for aggregation facets (channel/product breakdown), consider compound indexes that support both the match/filter and the group keys to reduce in-pipeline scanning and RU cost.
Enforce a JSON schema or document validation rules on collections (customers, events, cohort_snapshots) to catch malformed documents early and keep aggregation assumptions stable.
Prefer incremental or rolling snapshot updates (update only changed cohorts) rather than full recomputes when datasets are large, to reduce RU usage and snapshot run time.
